To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we developed a novel technique that enables us to grow out sufficient numbers of CD8+ cells from bronchial mucosa of smokers with COPD to examine their effector function; (2) these cells are predominantly CD8+/CD25+ and express CD69, CD28 and CD56; and (3) they exhibit cytotoxic activity against alveolar epithelial cells in vitro and express remodelling cytokine genes in vitro.

bronchial mucosa CD8+ T lymphocytes from patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases (COPD), particularly current smokers, have increased cytotoxic activity and cytokine production compared with controls, which suggests that these cells play a role in disease progression.

we have developed a novel approach to study the functional properties of bronchial T lymphocytes in COPD and have demonstrated increased cytotoxic activity in COPD smokers compared to controls, with increased expression of remodel‐ling cytokines in smokers with COPD compared to controls.
